headline: Wilderness River Permits and Lodge Bookings
reservation: Floating the Middle Fork or Main Salmon requires a highly competitive Four Rivers Lottery permit for peak season. Self-guided and commercial trips must be organized months in advance; verify current regulations with the Salmon-Challis National Forest official site.

days.title: The River of No Return Gorges

stops.name: Time Zone Rapid
stops.detail: Navigate the churning whitewater where the canyon walls drop steeply into the Salmon River.

stops.name: Lucile Recreation Site
stops.detail: A logical stop for beach access and observing the geological layers of the deep granite canyon.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours; conditions vary on narrow canyon roads
days.note: River conditions are subject to rapid change during spring melt; check local flow gauges daily.

days.title: Wilderness History and High Lookouts

stops.name: Sacajawea Heritage, Days, and Culture Center
stops.detail: Learn about the Agaidika Shoshone-Bannock people and the history of the Lewis and Clark Expedition.

stops.name: Jim Moore Place
stops.detail: Explore a historic riverside homestead accessible via hiking trails that showcase early canyon life.

days.driving: Walking or local boat transfer; conditions vary by trail
days.note: Carry ample water and sun protection as canyon trails offer little shade during midday.

days.title: Alpine Lakes and Sawtooth Headwaters

stops.name: Redfish Lake
stops.detail: Visit the glacial waters at the headwaters of the Salmon River under the jagged Sawtooth peaks.

stops.name: Salmon River Canyon Scenic Byway
stops.detail: Drive along the winding Highway 75 to see the river transition from alpine stream to powerful canyon force.

days.driving: Allow 2.5 hours; conditions vary with mountain weather
days.note: Stanley sits at high elevation; expect freezing temperatures even in summer mornings.

intel.title: Launch Site Congestion
intel.text: Parking at popular boat ramps like Corn Creek is extremely limited and prioritized for permit holders. Coordinate shuttle services in Salmon or Riggins to manage vehicle logistics.

intel.title: Remote Wilderness Blackout
intel.text: There is no cell service once you enter the Frank Church-River of No Return Wilderness. Satellite communication devices are recommended for those traveling outside of town centers.

intel.title: Crucial Supply Points
intel.text: Fuel is available in Riggins and Salmon, but there are no services for over 100 miles on some backcountry routes. Top off tanks before departing gateway cities.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Access
intel.text: Backcountry roads to remote river entry points may remain snow-blocked until late June. Consult the Salmon-Challis National Forest for seasonal gate opening dates.

intel.title: River Permit Checkpoints
intel.text: Rangers verify permits and mandatory gear at launch sites. Ensure you have the required fire pans and portable toilets to comply with wilderness regulations.

plan.arrival: Fly into Lewiston (LWS), collect a rental vehicle, and drive south to Riggins. Stock up on specialized river gear and groceries in Lewiston or Salmon before entering the canyon.
plan.vehicle: Consider a high-clearance 4WD for forest roads; standard vehicles are sufficient for the main paved byways between Stanley and Riggins.
plan.goldenHour: The cliffs at the Salmon River overlook near Stanley offer a view of the Sawtooth range, best during the late summer alpenglow.
